newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae to require disclosure on mortgage insurance.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae to require disclosure on mortgage insurance.

text.p: A Federal National Mortgage Association executive told a Senate panel on Tuesday it will require mortgage service companies to inform home buyers of the right to cancel private mortgage insurance when certain conditions are met.

"Fannie Mae is committed to ending any practice that results in homeowners paying for mortgage insurance that is not necessary," Fannie Mae Executive Vice President Ann Logan said in prepared testimony to the Senate Banking Committee.
Mortgage insurance is paid by borrowers with low down payments on their loans to protect lenders and mortgage investors from default.
Once borrowers have built up a certain amount of equity in their homes, they no longer need to pay insurance.

Fannie Mae said it now requires loan servicers -- companies which collect loan payments and distribute payments to investors -- to tell consumers, when a loan is taken out and annually, about private mortgage isurance, including how it can be cancelled when certain conditions are met.
Complaints have arisen that the mortgage industry has failed to notify many borrowers when their insurance obligation ceases, and has continued collecting payments from the uninformed borrowers.

"We have been reviewing our own policies and working with lenders, mortgage insurers and others on this issue, and in the weeks ahead we will communicate to servicers new policies requiring that consumers be fully informed about mortgage insurance and how it may be cancelled," Logan said.
Under the new policy, Fannie Mae also will require servicers to cancel insurance when a loan with good payment history reaches its "half-life," or halfway point of its duration.
Fannie Mae said it will continue allowing servicers to cancel insurance for borrowers with a good payment history when their loan balances fall to 80 percent of the home's original value.
Fannie Mae said it also will include a provision for homeowners to cancel insurance when the market value of their home increases to the point where the risk of default is diminished.
Fannie Mae is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
